doc.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023

title: Leaving the road for academia and family
summary: He wanted to raise a family; he talks about his degree-less career, his father, his wife Pat and daughter.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: What finally prompted you to consider leaving that life and entering what was very early jazz academia?

Right. Right you are. I wanted to raise a family. I mean I am the boy who came from academia in the first place. I never left academia. So that in a sense was always comfortable for me. I was always — I love people, period. I wanted to raise a family and make a living as a jazz trombone player and thanks to “Lonesome Old Town” I had a reputation all over the world. And I never got a degree myself, much to the discernment of my father, but I did get some honorary degrees a little later in life. So that made — the old man and I ended up good friends. So I have a wonderful family though. I think one of the most important things anybody could have is a family, a loving family too. And my wife Pat is a pianist from Indiana and I had to go through a divorce to get to some — really somebody I could live with and we’ll be married — we were married 55 years.

Yeah, yeah. And you could see, you just met my daughter, who is now 52 and she has seen us through the pandemic. You just don’t have daughters like that. She always — oh what do you call it — archivist. And she’s one hell of an archivist.
